Optimal.Notes: Native 1280x800 at medium-high settings is well within the Deck's capabilities for this game, giving a sharp, smooth experience. An 8 W TDP cap is enough to sustain 60 fps while keeping temperatures and fan noise low.

profiles.Summary: Mount & Blade: Warband is a 2010 lightweight 3D RPG with very modest PC requirements, making it an excellent fit for the Steam Deck — the hardware vastly outclasses the game's needs and stable 60 fps is easily achievable. It runs well under Proton (platinum tier) with no major compatibility hurdles reported.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's very modest 2010 PC requirements and the Deck's hardware capabilities. On your first run, verify the in-game resolution and shadow settings are applying correctly, and check fps in large battles where CPU-side unit AI is the most likely bottleneck.

MaxBattery.Notes: At 5 W TDP and a reduced render resolution the Deck barely breaks a sweat with this 2010 title, delivering excellent battery life. FSR sharpness 5 recovers most of the visual clarity lost at 960x600.

KnownIssues: No native controller support is stated; a community controller layout may be needed for comfortable play.
The game's UI was designed for mouse and keyboard, which can feel awkward on the Deck's small screen.
Multiplayer connectivity may occasionally require manual firewall or NAT workarounds under Proton.

MaxPerformance.Notes: With no TDP or frame cap the Deck runs Warband at maximum settings with ease, hitting the 60 Hz display ceiling in virtually all scenarios. Battery life shortens as the APU runs unconstrained, but performance headroom is enormous for this 2010 title.

Optimal.Notes: At native 1280x800 with high textures and moderate shadows, Warband runs comfortably at 60 fps on the Deck; large battles with many soldiers on screen may cause brief dips to the low 50s, which the 60 fps cap smooths out well.

profiles.Summary: Mount & Blade: Warband is a lightweight 2010 title with very modest PC requirements, running well within the Steam Deck's capabilities and achieving high frame rates even at native resolution. ProtonDB reports a platinum rating with strong confidence, meaning it runs smoothly under Proton with little to no configuration needed.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's 2010 PC minimum/recommended requirements (far below Deck hardware) and the platinum ProtonDB tier. On first run, check fps in a large siege battle — the busiest scenario — and drop shadow quality if it dips unexpectedly.

MaxBattery.Notes: This very old engine is extremely light on the GPU; a low clock and reduced render resolution with FSR upscaling keeps battery life exceptional. The game is simple enough that FSR artifacts are barely noticeable at this sharpness level.

KnownIssues: Controller/gamepad support may require remapping in Steam Input, as the game was primarily designed for mouse and keyboard.
Multiplayer functionality may have issues connecting to some servers under Proton.
The in-game cursor can behave oddly at non-standard resolutions or refresh rates on first launch.

MaxPerformance.Notes: The 2010 engine easily saturates the Deck at 90 Hz with all settings maxed; the only scenario where fps may drop below 90 is very large siege battles with 100+ combatants, where it may fall to the 70s. The OLED display at 90 Hz makes mounted combat feel noticeably smoother.
